 Advertisement First winter blast could bring snow to North Carolina mountains
 Advertisement Updated: 8:45 AM EST Nov 12, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Chris Justus Chief Meteorologist First winter blast could bring snow to North Carolina mountains
 Updated: 8:45 AM EST Nov 12, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Chris Justus Chief Meteorologist GREENVILLE, S.C. — The season’s first winter weather is taking shape, and it will send a blast of cold air across the entire East Coast. Behind that initial surge of cold, snow will be possible from the North Carolina mountains up the I-95 corridor into Vermont and Maine.
 File WYFF 4 WYFF News 4 Chief Meteorologist Chris Justus says everyone will feel the cold, but from the mountains of North Carolina northward, this is a snow event.
 Advertisement What to Know Right Now 
 What: The first widespread cold blast of the season, with accumulating snow in the North Carolina mountains.
 First snowfall expected in parts of the US — What's the earliest snow where you live? When: Thursday night through Saturday, followed by a cold weekend.
 Impacts: 3 to 5 inches of snow possible above 3,500 feet along the Tennessee – North Carolina state line, with a dusting to an inch at lower elevations in the mountains. Outside the mountains, expect the season’s first widespread frost and freeze.
 Timing and Storm Evolution 
 WYFF 4 
 The first batch of moisture and colder air moves in Thursday night and Friday. Here is what to expect:
 Temperatures stay cold throughout the day Friday
 As more moisture moves in, snow will intensify in the higher elevations Friday afternoon into the evening
 Snow peaks Friday night
 Snow tapers off throughout the day Saturday
 WYFF 4 To our north, snow will be possible up the I-95 corridor and into New England, with the heaviest totals expected across interior New York and Vermont.
 Who Sees Snow Here 
 WYFF 4 Closer to home, the snow stays in the mountains, and elevation makes all the difference:
 Above 3,500 feet: 3 to 5 inches possible along the Tennessee –North Carolina state line
 Lower elevations in the mountains: a dusting to an inch
 WYFF 4 
 If your travels take you from Asheville to Gatlinburg, you’ll at least see flurries. Going up and over on I-40, you’ll find some accumulation.
 A Cold Weekend 
 A cold weekend is on the way for everyone. The season’s first widespread frost and freeze outside of the mountains is likely.
 Weekend lows:
 Mid to upper 20s in the mountains
 30 to 33 degrees in the Upstate
 Is This Normal? 
 WYFF 4 Yes. This is all very normal. The average first frost and freeze outside of the mountains is Nov. 8, and the first snow in the mountains usually arrives around the same time. 
 November accounts for only about 2% of our yearly snowfall, but we do tend to get at least some action. The majority of our snow usually comes in the last two weeks of January and the first two weeks of February, though it can happen as late as March or April.
 Looking Ahead: The Winter Outlook
 Chris says to expect much of the same this winter. An El Niño weather pattern will make for an active southern jet stream, bringing multiple opportunities for rain. If cold air is nearby when those systems arrive, that means snow.
 Chris expects above-average snowfall this year for many areas from the Mid-Atlantic through the Carolinas and Georgia.
 Bottom Line 
 This is a cold blast for everyone and a snow event for the mountains, with the biggest totals above 3,500 feet. If you’re crossing the Tennessee – North Carolina line Friday or Saturday, plan for snow. Everyone else should get ready for the first frost and freeze of the season.

 About the WYFF News 4 weather team: 
 The WYFF News 4 weather team has been independently certified for having the most accurate forecast in the Greenville-Spartanburg-Asheville-Anderson market for the second year in a row.
 “Our goal every day, in every forecast, is accuracy,” said WYFF 4 President and General Manager Blake Bridges. “Our expert weather team is dedicated to giving viewers a forecast they can trust to be right. We are also the only station in the market with our own 24/7 live radar, Live Super Doppler 4. It’s clear that WYFF News 4 is the weather leader in this market.”
 The certification comes from WeatheRate, an independent research firm that tracks forecasts from every station in multiple markets across the country.
 “Everyone knows that forecasting the weather around here is difficult with the Upstate and mountains,” said WeatheRate President Bruce Fixman. “The station that gets the forecast right more than anyone else is Chief Meteorologist Chris Justus and the WYFF News 4 weather team.”
